C++ abstract interface for the OpenH264 SVC encoder. Provides lifecycle (Initialize/Uninitialize), configuration (SetOption/GetOption), and encoding APIs (EncodeFrame, EncodeParameterSets, ForceIntraFrame). Implemented by the library; client code uses pointers returned by WelsCreateSVCEncoder and must destroy via WelsDestroySVCEncoder.

C++ abstract interface for the OpenH264 decoder. Provides initialization, a set of decoding routines (including no-delay and parsing-only), flushing of remaining frames, and runtime options. Instances are created by WelsCreateDecoder and destroyed by WelsDestroyDecoder.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::Initialize
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI Initialize(const SEncParamBase* pParam) = 0;
functions.description: Initializes the OpenH264 encoder using basic parameters (SEncParamBase). Allocates internal resources and configures the encoder for subsequent EncodeFrame calls.
requirements: pParam must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SEncParamBase.
Fields in pParam (e.g., iUsageType, fMaxFrameRate, iPicWidth, iPicHeight, iTargetBitrate) must be set to valid values as required by the library.
Must be called before any other encoding operations (e.g., EncodeFrame).
If previously initialized, Uninitialize() should be called before re-initializing.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero indicates failure and the encoder should be considered uninitialized.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::InitializeExt
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI InitializeExt(const SEncParamExt* pParam) = 0;
functions.description: Initializes the encoder with extended parameters (SEncParamExt) to access advanced features such as multiple spatial layers and slice configuration.
requirements: pParam must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SEncParamExt.
Recommended usage is to call GetDefaultParams(&param) first, then modify fields as needed, then pass to InitializeExt.
If using SM_DYN_SLICE, note the example sets sSliceArgument.uiSliceSizeConstraint and uiMaxNalSize; multi-threading is not supported with SM_DYN_SLICE (as noted in comments).
Must be called before any encoding operations and after any prior Uninitialize() if reconfiguring.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero indicates failure and the encoder should be considered uninitialized.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::GetDefaultParams
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI GetDefaultParams(SEncParamExt* pParam) = 0;
functions.description: Fills an SEncParamExt structure with the encoder’s default extended parameters. Intended as a starting point before modifying fields and calling InitializeExt.
requirements: pParam must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SEncParamExt storage.
Call before InitializeExt to obtain defaults.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure (pParam contents undefined on failure).

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::Uninitialize
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI Uninitialize() = 0;
functions.description: Uninitializes the encoder and releases resources allocated during initialization.
requirements: Call after finishing encoding to free resources.
Must not be called concurrently with other encoder operations.
After Uninitialize, the encoder instance must be re-initialized before reuse.
Return 0 on success; nonzero indicates failure (state unknown).

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::EncodeFrame
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI EncodeFrame(const SSourcePicture* kpSrcPic, SFrameBSInfo* pBsInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Encodes a single input frame (I420) into H.264 bitstream output. On success, pBsInfo contains the encoded NAL units and frame metadata.
requirements: kpSrcPic must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SSourcePicture describing the input frame.
Input color format should be I420 as per comments; ensure iColorFormat is set accordingly and strides (iStride[0..2]) and dimensions (iPicWidth/iPicHeight) are set consistently.
The chroma planes must be laid out as: Cb at Y + width*height, Cr after Cb with size (width*height)/4 (I420). The caller must ensure buffer validity and correct layout.
pBsInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SFrameBSInfo.
Encoder must be successfully initialized before calling.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero indicates failure. Frames may be skipped (check info.eFrameType for videoFrameTypeSkip in typical usage).

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::EncodeParameterSets
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI EncodeParameterSets(SFrameBSInfo* pBsInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Generates and outputs codec parameter sets (e.g., SPS/PPS) into the provided bitstream info buffer without encoding a video frame.
requirements: pBsInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SFrameBSInfo.
Encoder must be initialized before calling.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::ForceIntraFrame
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI ForceIntraFrame(bool bIDR, int iLayerId = -1) = 0;
functions.description: Forces the next encoded frame to be an IDR frame when bIDR is true. If bIDR is false, returns 1 and does nothing. Optional iLayerId can target a specific spatial layer (default -1 for all/unspecified).
requirements: Encoder must be initialized before calling.
bIDR=true requests an IDR; bIDR=false results in return value 1 and no action (per comments).
iLayerId meaning and valid range are not detailed in this header; when unknown, use the default -1.
Returns 0 on success forcing IDR; 1 if bIDR is false; other nonzero values indicate failure.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::SetOption
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI SetOption(ENCODER_OPTION eOptionId, void* pOption) = 0;
functions.description: Sets an encoder option identified by ENCODER_OPTION. Used for runtime configuration such as input data format, IDR interval, frame rate, bitrate, or other encoder parameters.
requirements: Encoder must be initialized for options that affect active encoding; some options may be set before initialization depending on the specific option (not detailed here).
eOptionId must be a valid ENCODER_OPTION value.
pOption must be a valid pointer to a value/structure matching the expected type for the specified eOptionId (consult ENCODER_OPTION documentation).
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure.

functions.name: ISVCEncoder::GetOption
functions.signature: virtual int EXTAPI GetOption(ENCODER_OPTION eOptionId, void* pOption) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the current value of an encoder option identified by ENCODER_OPTION.
requirements: eOptionId must be a valid ENCODER_OPTION value.
pOption must be non-null and point to writable storage of the correct type/size expected for the option.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure; on failure, contents of pOption are undefined.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::Initialize
functions.signature: virtual long EXTAPI Initialize(const SDecodingParam* pParam) = 0;
functions.description: Initializes the OpenH264 decoder with decoding parameters, allocating internal state and resources. Supports both full decoding and parse-only modes depending on parameters.
requirements: pParam must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized SDecodingParam.
If parse-only mode is desired, set pParam->bParseOnly=true (as shown in usage example).
Decoder must be initialized before any Decode* or GetOption/SetOption that require an active decoder.
Returns 0 on success; nonzero indicates failure.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::Uninitialize
functions.signature: virtual long EXTAPI Uninitialize() = 0;
functions.description: Uninitializes the decoder and releases all associated resources.
requirements: Call after all decoding work is finished.
Must not be called concurrently with Decode* or option operations.
After Uninitialize, Initialize must be called before reuse.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::DecodeFrame
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI DecodeFrame(const unsigned char* pSrc, const int iSrcLen, unsigned char** ppDst, int* pStride, int& iWidth, int& iHeight) = 0;
functions.description: Decodes one frame from the provided H.264 bitstream. On success, outputs planar I420 YUV buffers, per-plane strides, and image dimensions.
requirements: pSrc may be null and iSrcLen 0 in certain draining scenarios is not documented for this variant; normally provide a valid bitstream pointer including start code prefixes, and a positive iSrcLen.
ppDst must point to an array of at least 3 uint8_t* entries for Y, U, V output buffers.
pStride must be a valid, non-null pointer to storage for per-plane stride values; exact count not specified here (at least 2–3 entries typical for I420).
iWidth and iHeight are output references that must be valid lvalues to receive the decoded dimensions.
Decoder must be initialized before calling.
Return is a DECODING_STATE; 0 indicates success; nonzero indicates errors or special states.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::DecodeFrameNoDelay
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI DecodeFrameNoDelay(const unsigned char* pSrc, const int iSrcLen, unsigned char** ppDst, SBufferInfo* pDstInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Slice-level decoding that parses and reconstructs a complete input frame immediately when possible. Recommended as the main decoding API for H.264/AVC input. Output is available only when pDstInfo->iBufferStatus == 1.
requirements: pSrc should point to the H.264 bytestream (including start codes); iSrcLen is its length.
ppDst must point to an array of at least 3 uint8_t* entries for Y, U, V output buffers.
pDstInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SBufferInfo. Output I420 data is valid only if pDstInfo->iBufferStatus == 1.
Decoder must be initialized before calling.
Return is DECODING_STATE; caller must handle nonzero values and use pDstInfo->iBufferStatus to determine output availability.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::DecodeFrame2
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI DecodeFrame2(const unsigned char* pSrc, const int iSrcLen, unsigned char** ppDst, SBufferInfo* pDstInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Slice-level decoding that may buffer slices until a full picture is reconstructed. Output is only available when pDstInfo->iBufferStatus == 1 (e.g., after receiving all slices of a frame).
requirements: pSrc may be NULL with iSrcLen == 0 to trigger no-delay reconstruction/drain previously queued data (as shown in example).
Otherwise, pSrc must point to H.264 bitstream data; iSrcLen is its length.
ppDst must point to an array of at least 3 uint8_t* entries for Y, U, V output buffers.
pDstInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SBufferInfo; check iBufferStatus==1 to use ppDst contents.
Decoder must be initialized before calling.
Return is DECODING_STATE; caller must handle errors and check iBufferStatus for output.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::FlushFrame
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI FlushFrame(unsigned char** ppDst, SBufferInfo* pDstInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves a ready decoded frame remaining in internal buffers after the last input was decoded (buffer drain). Applicable only for streams with profile_idc != 66. Use GetOption with DECODER_OPTION_NUM_OF_FRAMES_REMAINING_IN_BUFFER to query pending frames.
requirements: ppDst must point to an array of at least 3 uint8_t* entries for Y, U, V output buffers.
pDstInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SBufferInfo; output is available when pDstInfo->iBufferStatus == 1.
Only applicable when the stream profile_idc != 66 (as noted).
Decoder must be initialized before calling.
Return is DECODING_STATE; caller must check pDstInfo->iBufferStatus for output availability.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::DecodeParser
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI DecodeParser(const unsigned char* pSrc, const int iSrcLen, SParserBsInfo* pDstInfo) = 0;
functions.description: Parses input bitstream only (no picture reconstruction) and rewrites any SVC syntax to AVC syntax. Intended for parse-only workflows (e.g., hardware decoding handoff).
requirements: pSrc must point to the H.264 bitstream; iSrcLen is its length.

pDstInfo must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SParserBsInfo. The caller must allocate sufficient buffer space in pDstInfo->pDstBuff to hold the transcoded bitstream for a frame (as in example).
When using parse-only mode, configure the decoder with SDecodingParam.bParseOnly=true during Initialize.
Return is DECODING_STATE; nonzero indicates errors or special states.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::DecodeFrameEx
functions.signature: virtual DECODING_STATE EXTAPI DecodeFrameEx(const unsigned char* pSrc, const int iSrcLen, unsigned char* pDst, int iDstStride, int& iDstLen, int& iWidth, int& iHeight, int& iColorFormat) = 0;
functions.description: Experimental/future API intended to support non-I420 color format output. The header notes that this API does not work for now.
requirements: Function is documented as not working currently; behavior is undefined.

If used, pSrc/iSrcLen should describe input bytestream; pDst must point to sufficient writable output buffer with stride iDstStride; iDstLen, iWidth, iHeight, iColorFormat are output references that must be valid lvalues.
Because it is not supported, callers should avoid relying on this API.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::SetOption
functions.signature: virtual long EXTAPI SetOption(DECODER_OPTION eOptionId, void* pOption) = 0;
functions.description: Sets a decoder option identified by DECODER_OPTION (e.g., output data format, EOS flag, error concealment mode).
requirements: eOptionId must be a valid DECODER_OPTION value.
pOption must be a valid pointer to a value/structure matching the specified option’s expected type.
Decoder must be initialized for options that affect active decoding; some options may be allowed pre-initialize depending on the specific option (not detailed here).
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure.

functions.name: ISVCDecoder::GetOption
functions.signature: virtual long EXTAPI GetOption(DECODER_OPTION eOptionId, void* pOption) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the current value of a decoder option identified by DECODER_OPTION.
requirements: eOptionId must be a valid DECODER_OPTION value.
pOption must be non-null and point to writable storage of the correct type/size for the requested option.
Decoder should be initialized when querying options that depend on runtime state.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure; on failure, contents of pOption are undefined.

functions.name: WelsCreateSVCEncoder
functions.signature: int WelsCreateSVCEncoder(ISVCEncoder** ppEncoder);
functions.description: Creates an encoder instance and returns it via ppEncoder.
requirements: ppEncoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the created ISVCEncoder*.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure. On failure, *ppEncoder is unspecified and should not be used.
Caller is responsible for destroying the encoder with WelsDestroySVCEncoder after use.

functions.name: WelsDestroySVCEncoder
functions.signature: void WelsDestroySVCEncoder(ISVCEncoder* pEncoder);
functions.description: Destroys an encoder instance previously created by WelsCreateSVCEncoder.
requirements: pEncoder must be a pointer returned by WelsCreateSVCEncoder (or NULL if the caller chooses to no-op).
Encoder should be Uninitialize()'d prior to destruction (as per example).
Must not be called concurrently with other operations on the same encoder.

functions.name: WelsGetDecoderCapability
functions.signature: int WelsGetDecoderCapability(SDecoderCapability* pDecCapability);
functions.description: Queries decoder capabilities and writes them into the provided SDecoderCapability struct.
requirements: pDecCapability must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable SDecoderCapability.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure.

functions.name: WelsCreateDecoder
functions.signature: long WelsCreateDecoder(ISVCDecoder** ppDecoder);
functions.description: Creates a decoder instance and returns it via ppDecoder.
requirements: ppDecoder must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the created ISVCDecoder*.
Returns 0 on success; otherwise failure. On failure, *ppDecoder is unspecified.
Caller is responsible for destroying the decoder with WelsDestroyDecoder after use.

functions.name: WelsDestroyDecoder
functions.signature: void WelsDestroyDecoder(ISVCDecoder* pDecoder);
functions.description: Destroys a decoder instance previously created by WelsCreateDecoder.
requirements: pDecoder must be a pointer returned by WelsCreateDecoder (or NULL if the caller chooses to no-op).
Decoder should be Uninitialize()'d prior to destruction (as per example).
Must not be called concurrently with other operations on the same decoder.

functions.name: WelsGetCodecVersion
functions.signature: OpenH264Version WelsGetCodecVersion(void);

data_types.description: Three separate buffers containing a single video frame in planar I420 (a.k.a. YUV 4:2:0, I420) layout: Y plane of size width*height, followed by U (Cb) plane of size (width/2)*(height/2), and V (Cr) plane of size (width/2)*(height/2). Each plane is independent in memory here (not a single concatenated buffer). Strides typically equal plane widths. Byte values are unconstrained 0–255.

An H.264/AVC elementary stream byte sequence suitable for decoder input, typically composed of one or more NAL units prefixed with start codes (Annex B format). Contents may include SPS/PPS, IDR/non-IDR slices, SEI, etc. Arbitrary length from empty to multiple NALs.

import random
from typing import List

# Target data type: raw I420 planes (separate Y, U, V buffers)
# Fuzzer stub expectations:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used three times to supply separate buffers for Y, U, V.
# - The stub then resizes each string to the exact plane size: Y = w*h, U = (w/2)*(h/2), V = (w/2)*(h/2).
# - Width/height are taken from encoder attributes; if unavailable, defaults w=h=16.
# Our generator will therefore emit a single bytes blob that the harness will split/consume
# in order across FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We make the blob a concatenation of three planes
# matching a small, common resolution to maximize validity when attributes are unknown.
# We choose 16x16 by default (matches stub fallback), but vary content patterns with seed.

MAX_BYTES = 4096


def _build_planes(w: int, h: int, mode: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compute plane sizes
    y_w, y_h = w, h
    uv_w, uv_h = w // 2, h // 2
    y_size = y_w * y_h
    uv_size = uv_w * uv_h

    # Helper patterns to generate interesting valid video content
    def solid(value: int, n: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes([value & 0xFF]) * n

    def horizontal_gradient(width: int, height: int, start: int, end: int) -> bytes:
        # left-to-right gradient repeated for each row
        if width <= 1:
            row = bytes([start & 0xFF])
            return row * height
        line = bytearray(width)
        for x in range(width):
            v = start + (end - start) * x // (width - 1)
            line[x] = v & 0xFF
        return bytes(line) * height

    def checker(width: int, height: int, v0: int, v1: int, block: int) -> bytes:
        buf = bytearray(width * height)
        for y in range(height):
            for x in range(width):
                vx = (x // max(1, block)) & 1
                vy = (y // max(1, block)) & 1
                buf[y * width + x] = (v0 if (vx ^ vy) == 0 else v1) & 0xFF
        return bytes(buf)

    def noise(n: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

    # Choose pattern mode to diversify yet remain valid
    # 0: solid gray + neutral chroma
    # 1: luma gradient, neutral chroma
    # 2: checkerboard luma, alternating chroma
    # 3: random noise for all planes
    # 4: color tint via chroma bias
    m = mode % 5
    if m == 0:
        y = solid(128, y_size)
        u = solid(128, uv_size)
        v = solid(128, uv_size)
    elif m == 1:
        y = horizontal_gradient(y_w, y_h, 16, 235)
        u = solid(128, uv_size)
        v = solid(128, uv_size)
    elif m == 2:
        blk = max(1, min(y_w, y_h) // 4)
        y = checker(y_w, y_h, 32, 224, blk)
        u = checker(uv_w, uv_h, 96, 160, max(1, blk // 2))
        v = checker(uv_w, uv_h, 96, 160, max(1, blk // 2))
    elif m == 3:
        y = noise(y_size)
        u = noise(uv_size)
        v = noise(uv_size)
    else:
        # slight color tint: blue-ish or red-ish depending on seed
        tint = rng.choice([("blue", (192, 96)), ("red", (96, 192))])[1]
        y = horizontal_gradient(y_w, y_h, 64, 200)
        u = solid(tint[0], uv_size)
        v = solid(tint[1], uv_size)

    return y + u + v


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # The fuzzer stub defaults to w=h=16 if encoder attrs are absent.
    # Keep sizes small to stay under 2KB and within the stub expectations.
    # Occasionally vary between a few legal even dims that still downsample cleanly.
    dims: List[int] = [16, 32]  # Even values; but 16 aligns with stub default
    # Prefer 16x16 most of the time to maximize validity when encoder uses defaults.
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        w = h = 16
    else:
        w = rng.choice(dims)
        h = rng.choice(dims)

    # Build planes with a deterministic yet varied pattern based on seed
    mode = rng.randrange(0, 5)
    payload = _build_planes(w, h, mode, rng)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(payload) > MAX_BYTES:
        payload = payload[:MAX_BYTES]

    return payload

import random
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a valid H.264 Annex B bytestream composed of SPS/PPS and one IDR slice.
# It targets the ISVCDecoder::* fuzz stubs which take FUZZ_PARAM_STR as the bitstream input.
# The produced streams are small, self-contained, and vary aspects like profile/level, resolution,
# and presence of SEI AUD, while remaining decodable by typical H.264 decoders (OpenH264).
#
# Notes:
# - We emit Annex B start codes (0x00000001) before each NAL.
# - We construct minimal, plausible SPS and PPS payloads (baseline/main/high, common levels).
# - We generate a single IDR slice with a very simple payload (does not aim to be a full compliant
#   bitstream, but commonly accepted by tolerant decoders that parse headers; OpenH264 is permissive
#   enough for small synthetic frames). We keep nal_ref_idc high for SPS/PPS/IDR.
# - We sometimes prepend AUD and/or SEI to exercise parser paths.
# - We ensure bytestream length <= 4096 bytes.

# Utility: Exp-Golomb encoding (unsigned)
def ue(v: int) -> List[int]:
    if v < 0:
        v = 0
    code_num = v + 1
    # binary of code_num
    b = bin(code_num)[2:]
    prefix_zeros = len(b) - 1
    bits = [0] * prefix_zeros + [1] + [int(x) for x in b[1:]]
    return bits

# Utility: write bits into bytes with rbsp trailing bits handling to byte-align
class BitWriter:
    def __init__(self):
        self.bits: List[int] = []
    def write_bits(self, bits: List[int]):
        self.bits.extend(bits)
    def write_bit(self, b: int):
        self.bits.append(1 if b else 0)
    def write_u(self, value: int, nbits: int):
        for i in reversed(range(nbits)):
            self.write_bit((value >> i) & 1)
    def write_ue(self, v: int):
        self.write_bits(ue(v))
    def rbsp_trailing_bits(self):
        # rbsp_stop_one_bit (1) then zero pad to next byte
        self.write_bit(1)
        while len(self.bits) % 8 != 0:
            self.write_bit(0)
    def get_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        out = bytearray()
        b = 0
        cnt = 0
        for bit in self.bits:
            b = (b << 1) | (bit & 1)
            cnt += 1
            if cnt == 8:
                out.append(b)
                b = 0
                cnt = 0
        if cnt != 0:
            out.append(b << (8 - cnt))
        return bytes(out)

# Escape 0x000003 prevention three bytes in RBSP->EBSP conversion
def rbsp_to_ebsp(rbsp: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    zeros = 0
    for ch in rbsp:
        if zeros >= 2 and ch <= 3:
            out.append(0x03)
            zeros = 0
        out.append(ch)
        if ch == 0x00:
            zeros += 1
        else:
            zeros = 0
    return bytes(out)

def nal(startcode: bytes, nal_ref_idc: int, nal_unit_type: int, rbsp_payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    hdr = bytes([((nal_ref_idc & 0x3) << 5) | (nal_unit_type & 0x1F)])
    ebsp = rbsp_to_ebsp(rbsp_payload)
    return startcode + hdr + ebsp

def make_sps(profile_idc: int, level_idc: int, width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal SPS (constraint flags set to 0), log2_max_frame_num_minus4=0, pic_order_cnt_type=2,
    # num_ref_frames=1, frame_mbs_only_flag=1, no cropping, square PAR
    bw = BitWriter()
    # profile_idc (8), constraint flags+reserved (8), level_idc (8)
    sps_header = bytes([profile_idc & 0xFF, 0x00, level_idc & 0xFF])
    # seq_parameter_set_id = 0
    bw.write_ue(0)
    # log2_max_frame_num_minus4 = 0 (=> max_frame_num=16)
    bw.write_ue(0)
    # pic_order_cnt_type = 2
    bw.write_ue(2)
    # if type 2: no further POC fields
    # max_num_ref_frames = 1
    bw.write_ue(1)
    # gaps_in_frame_num_value_allowed_flag = 0
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # picture size in macroblocks
    pic_width_in_mbs_minus1 = max(0, (width + 15) // 16 - 1)
    pic_height_in_map_units_minus1 = max(0, (height + 15) // 16 - 1)
    bw.write_ue(pic_width_in_mbs_minus1)
    bw.write_ue(pic_height_in_map_units_minus1)
    # frame_mbs_only_flag = 1 (no interlace)
    bw.write_bit(1)
    # direct_8x8_inference_flag = 1
    bw.write_bit(1)
    # frame_cropping_flag = 0
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # vui_parameters_present_flag = 0 (keep minimal)
    bw.write_bit(0)
    bw.rbsp_trailing_bits()
    rbsp = sps_header + bw.get_bytes()
    return nal(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01", 3, 7, rbsp)

def make_pps() -> bytes:
    # Minimal PPS: pps_id=0, sps_id=0, entropy_coding_mode_flag=0 (CAVLC), pic_order_present_flag=0,
    # num_slice_groups_minus1=0, num_ref_idx_l0/1_default_active_minus1=0, weighted_pred flags 0,
    # pic_init_qp_minus26=0, deblocking params default, more flags 0
    bw = BitWriter()
    bw.write_ue(0)  # pic_parameter_set_id
    bw.write_ue(0)  # seq_parameter_set_id
    bw.write_bit(0)  # entropy_coding_mode_flag
    bw.write_bit(0)  # pic_order_present_flag
    bw.write_ue(0)   # num_slice_groups_minus1
    bw.write_ue(0)   # num_ref_idx_l0_default_active_minus1
    bw.write_ue(0)   # num_ref_idx_l1_default_active_minus1
    bw.write_bit(0)  # weighted_pred_flag
    bw.write_u(0, 2) # weighted_bipred_idc
    bw.write_ue(0)   # pic_init_qp_minus26
    bw.write_ue(0)   # pic_init_qs_minus26
    bw.write_ue(0)   # chroma_qp_index_offset
    bw.write_bit(0)  # deblocking_filter_control_present_flag
    bw.write_bit(0)  # constrained_intra_pred_flag
    bw.write_bit(0)  # redundant_pic_cnt_present_flag
    bw.rbsp_trailing_bits()
    rbsp = bw.get_bytes()
    return nal(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01", 3, 8, rbsp)

def make_aud(primary_pic_type: int) -> bytes:
    # Access Unit Delimiter: primary_pic_type (3 bits), rbsp_trailing_bits
    bw = BitWriter()
    bw.write_u(primary_pic_type & 0x7, 3)
    bw.rbsp_trailing_bits()
    return nal(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01", 0, 9, bw.get_bytes())

def make_sei_user_data_unregistered(payload_len: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # SEI type 5 (user_data_unregistered) with 16-byte UUID + payload
    payload_type = 5
    payload_size = 16 + payload_len
    # write payloadType as 0xFF chunks then remainder
    header = bytearray()
    while payload_type >= 255:
        header.append(255)
        payload_type -= 255
    header.append(payload_type)
    size = payload_size
    while size >= 255:
        header.append(255)
        size -= 255
    header.append(size)
    uuid = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(16))
    payload = uuid + bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(payload_len))
    rbsp = bytes(header) + payload + b"\x80"  # rbsp trailing bits (1000 0000)
    return nal(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01", 0, 6, rbsp)

def make_idr_slice(width: int, height: int, qp: int, idr_pic_id: int) -> bytes:
    # Very simple IDR slice with I-slice, first_mb_in_slice=0, slice_type=I, pps_id=0,
    # frame_num=0, idr_pic_id, no ref pics, no deblocking params, etc.
    # This is intentionally minimalistic but commonly acceptable by OpenH264 for small frames.
    bw = BitWriter()
    # slice_header
    bw.write_ue(0)  # first_mb_in_slice
    bw.write_ue(2)  # slice_type: 2 -> I (some decoders accept 2 or 7 for all I)
    bw.write_ue(0)  # pic_parameter_set_id
    # frame_num with log2_max_frame_num_minus4=0 => 4 bits, write 0
    bw.write_u(0, 4)
    # idr_pic_flag assumed via nal_unit_type=5 -> write idr_pic_id ue
    bw.write_ue(idr_pic_id & 0x1F)
    # pic_order_cnt_type=2 -> no pic_order_cnt_lsb
    # redundant_pic_cnt_present_flag=0
    # direct_spatial_mv_pred_flag absent for I-slice
    # num_ref_idx_active_override_flag=0
    bw.write_bit(0)
    # ref_pic_list_modification_flag_l0=0 for I-slice not present
    # pred_weight_table not present for I-slice
    # dec_ref_pic_marking: no_long_term -> write no_output_of_prior_pics_flag=0, long_term_reference_flag=0
    bw.write_bit(0)  # no_output_of_prior_pics_flag
    bw.write_bit(0)  # long_term_reference_flag
    # slice_qp_delta relative to pic_init_qp_minus26 (we set pps init qp = 26), so delta = qp-26
    bw.write_ue(max(0, qp - 26))
    # rbsp trailing bits
    bw.rbsp_trailing_bits()
    rbsp = bw.get_bytes()
    return nal(b"\x00\x00\x00\x01", 3, 5, rbsp)

def choose_profile_level(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    profiles = [66, 77, 100]  # Baseline, Main, High
    levels = [10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 30, 31, 32, 40, 41]
    return rng.choice(profiles), rng.choice(levels)

def choose_size(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    sizes = [
        (16, 16), (32, 32), (64, 64),
        (80, 48), (96, 64), (128, 72), (128, 96),
        (160, 90), (176, 144), (240, 136), (320, 180), (320, 240),
        (352, 288), (368, 208), (426, 240)
    ]
    return rng.choice(sizes)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    prof, lvl = choose_profile_level(rng)
    w, h = choose_size(rng)
    qp = rng.randrange(22, 36)
    idr_id = rng.randrange(0, 16)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Optionally add AUD
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        primary_pic_type = rng.randrange(0, 3)  # I or I/P
        parts.append(make_aud(primary_pic_type))

    # Optionally add a small SEI user_data_unregistered
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sei_len = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        parts.append(make_sei_user_data_unregistered(sei_len, rng))

    parts.append(make_sps(prof, lvl, w, h))
    parts.append(make_pps())
    parts.append(make_idr_slice(w, h, qp, idr_id))

    bs = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure within size limit
    if len(bs) > 4096:
        bs = bs[:4096]
    return bs
